title: fix: clamp inverted visible range in ListView to prevent RangeError (fixes #333230)
body:
### Summary `RangeError: Invalid array length` is thrown in `ListView.probeDynamicHeights` (`src/vs/base/browser/ui/list/listView.ts`) when it evaluates `new Array(range.end - range.start)` with an **inverted range** (`end < start`). The negative length throws immediately. The inverted range originates in `getVisibleRange(renderTop, renderHeight)`. When the viewport is collapsed or hidden during a layout pass (`renderHeight <= 0`), the expression `renderTop + renderHeight - 1` becomes smaller than `renderTop`. Because `rangeMap.indexAfter(position) = min(indexAt(position) + 1, count)` is monotonic in `position`, the resulting `end` can resolve to an index **before** `start`, yielding `{ start, end }` with `end < start`. This malformed `IRange` violates the `start <= end` invariant that consumers assume. This is a recent regression (new bucket in 1.135.0, 411 users): the previous `_rerender` iterated with `for (let i = range.start; i < range.end; i++)`, which silently tolerated an inverted range by not iterating. The batched-measurement rewrite replaced that loop with an eagerly-sized array, turning the previously-harmless inverted range into a hard crash. Fixes microsoft/vscode#333230 Recommended reviewer: `@connor4312` ### Culprit Commit `c2b336daae7101676f179b30f92641cdfcc6b38c` — "list: batch dynamic height measurements (#330967)" by Connor Peet (`connor4312`), 2026-08-18. This commit falls within the reported regression range (`0d0c8a6...68161d9`, 1.134.0-insider → 1.135.0-insider) and introduced `probeDynamicHeights`, which allocates `new Array(range.end - range.start)` without guaranteeing `end >= start`. ### Code Flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[layout / setScrollDimensions with renderHeight <= 0] --> B[onScroll] B --> C[_rerender] C --> D["getVisibleRange(renderTop, renderHeight)"] D --> E["end = indexAfter(renderTop + renderHeight - 1)
can be < start when renderHeight ≤ 0"] E --> F["inverted IRange: end < start"] F --> G["probeDynamicHeights(range)"] G --> H["new Array(range.end - range.start)
negative length"] H --> I["RangeError: Invalid array length"] ``` ### Affected Files - `src/vs/base/browser/ui/list/listView.ts` — `getVisibleRange` (producer of the inverted range) and `probeDynamicHeights` (crash site). ### Repro Steps Not reliably reproducible via manual steps; occurs under a layout race. Conceptually: 1. Host a `ListView` inside a widget whose container can be laid out with zero/negative height (e.g., a collapsed chat/inline-chat widget). 2. Trigger a layout/scroll pass while `renderHeight <= 0`. 3. `getVisibleRange` returns an inverted range; `probeDynamicHeights` allocates a negative-length array and throws `RangeError: Invalid array length`. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `src/vs/base/browser/ui/list/listView.ts`, `getVisibleRange`: compute `start` first, then clamp `end` with `Math.max(start, indexAfter(renderTop + renderHeight - 1))`. This fixes the bug at the data producer rather than at the crash site: `getVisibleRange` constructs the `IRange`, so enforcing the `start <= end` invariant there guarantees every consumer (including `probeDynamicHeights`) receives a well-formed range. An empty range (`start === end`) is valid and yields a zero-length array, restoring the harmless behavior the previous `for`-loop had. After this change, `getVisibleRange` cannot produce a range with `end < start` because `end` is explicitly clamped to be at least `start`, so `range.end - range.start` is always `>= 0` and `new Array(...)` can no longer receive a negative length. **Alternatives considered:** - Guard at the crash site in `probeDynamicHeights` (e.g., early-return or clamp the array length there) — rejected because it patches the symptom at the bottom of the stack while leaving the malformed `IRange` flowing to every other consumer; the fix must live where the invalid data is produced. ### Recommended Owner `connor4312` (Connor Peet) — authored the culprit commit `c2b336daae71` and is an active repository collaborator with recent commits. > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/33202685801) · opus48 · 452.1 AIC · ⌖ 11.3 AIC · ⊞ 18.6K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests)

title: fix: revive telemetryInfo.sessionResource on chat editing timeline restore (fixes #333229)
body:
### Summary `isAgentHostSessionResource(this._telemetryInfo.sessionResource)` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'scheme')` because `sessionResource` is `undefined`, violating its non-nullable `readonly sessionResource: URI` contract. The invalid value originates when a chat editing session's **checkpoint timeline** is persisted and restored: the telemetry info objects are getter-backed anonymous class instances, and `JSON.stringify` drops their prototype getters, so the restored objects lack `sessionResource`. The snapshot restore path already re-injects the session resource, but the timeline restore path did not. This fix re-injects the owning `chatSessionResource` into timeline-restored telemetry info, mirroring the snapshot path. Fixes microsoft/vscode#333229 Recommended reviewer: `@connor4312` ### Culprit Commit `8f4fc8d3273653bfb73b8d4c3cfc7eeecd00722c` — "chat: identify Agent Host telemetry sessions (#332000)" by Connor Peet (copeet@microsoft.com), Aug 21 2026. This commit introduced the `isAgentHostSessionResource(this._telemetryInfo.sessionResource)` call in `chatEditingModifiedFileEntry.ts`, which newly dereferences `.scheme` on a `sessionResource` that can be `undefined` after a timeline restore. Shipped in commit `08d4889f9ec4a1685d257b9b95de036c8e1ce1e5` (Version 1.135.0, last seen Aug 27 2026); the culprit (Aug 21) is an ancestor of the shipped build (Aug 27). ### Code Flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[_getTelemetryInfoForModel
chatEditingSession.ts:1030] -->|anonymous class
getter-based sessionResource| B[telemetryInfo on operations & fileBaselines] B --> C[getStateForPersistence
chatEditingCheckpointTimelineImpl.ts] C -->|JSON.stringify drops
prototype getters| D[persisted timeline state
sessionResource lost] D --> E[restoreFromState
operations/baselines rehydrated
sessionResource = undefined] E --> F[_notifyAction
chatEditingModifiedFileEntry.ts:277] F --> G[isAgentHostSessionResource
chatSessionsService.ts:405] G -->|resource.scheme| H[TypeError: reading 'scheme'] ``` ### Affected Files - `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatEditing/chatEditingCheckpointTimelineImpl.ts` — timeline restore path; the fix re-injects `sessionResource` here. - `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatEditing/chatEditingModifiedFileEntry.ts` (crash site, line 277) — unchanged; not the correct fix location. - `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/chatSessionsService.ts` (line 405, throw site) — unchanged. - `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatEditing/chatEditingSession.ts` (line 1030, producer of getter-based telemetry info) — unchanged. ### Repro Steps 1. Start a chat editing session that produces file operations/baselines (edits with an agent). 2. Persist the session so its checkpoint timeline state is serialized via `JSON.stringify`. 3. Reload the window so the timeline is restored via `restoreFromState`; the restored `telemetryInfo.sessionResource` is `undefined` because the getter was dropped during serialization. 4. Trigger a session action (`_notifyAction`), which calls `isAgentHostSessionResource(this._telemetryInfo.sessionResource)` → `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'scheme')`. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** (`chatEditingCheckpointTimelineImpl.ts`): In `restoreFromState`, restored `operations` (Create ops) and `fileBaselines` now pass their `telemetryInfo` through a new `_reviveTelemetryInfo` helper that re-injects the timeline's own `chatSessionResource` when `sessionResource` is missing. This fixes the data at the restore boundary — the actual producer of the invalid value — rather than guarding the crash site. The bypass is the `JSON.stringify` round-trip that silently drops the getter-backed `sessionResource` (declared non-nullable `URI`), and the restore boundary is where the type contract must be re-established. This mirrors the existing snapshot restore path, which already re-injects `this._chatSessionResource`. After this change, `restoreFromState` cannot yield a `telemetryInfo` with an undefined `sessionResource`, because every restored operation/baseline telemetry info is passed through `_reviveTelemetryInfo`, which substitutes the timeline's `chatSessionResource` whenever the deserialized value is missing. **Alternatives considered:** - Add `?.` / a guard at the crash site (`chatEditingModifiedFileEntry.ts:277`) — rejected because it masks the symptom at the consumer instead of fixing the data producer, leaving `sessionResource` `undefined` for every other consumer and violating the non-nullable contract silently. - Change the producer `_getTelemetryInfoForModel` to use own enumerable properties instead of getters — rejected because the getters are intentional (the response result is not available when editing starts), and it would not repair already-persisted state. ### Recommended Owner `@connor4312` (Connor Peet) — author of the culprit commit `8f4fc8d3`, active collaborator (recent commit Aug 27 2026), and owner of the Agent Host telemetry session code. > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/33202683766) · opus48 · 623.6 AIC · ⌖ 12 AIC · ⊞ 18.6K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests)

title: fix: clamp inverted visible range in ListView to prevent RangeError (fixes #333230)
body:
### Summary `RangeError: Invalid array length` is thrown in `ListView.probeDynamicHeights` (`src/vs/base/browser/ui/list/listView.ts`) when it evaluates `new Array(range.end - range.start)` with an **inverted range** (`end < start`). The negative length throws immediately. The inverted range originates in `getVisibleRange(renderTop, renderHeight)`. When the viewport is collapsed or hidden during a layout pass (`renderHeight <= 0`), the expression `renderTop + renderHeight - 1` becomes smaller than `renderTop`. Because `rangeMap.indexAfter(position) = min(indexAt(position) + 1, count)` is monotonic in `position`, the resulting `end` can resolve to an index **before** `start`, yielding `{ start, end }` with `end < start`. This malformed `IRange` violates the `start <= end` invariant that consumers assume. This is a recent regression (new bucket in 1.135.0, 411 users): the previous `_rerender` iterated with `for (let i = range.start; i < range.end; i++)`, which silently tolerated an inverted range by not iterating. The batched-measurement rewrite replaced that loop with an eagerly-sized array, turning the previously-harmless inverted range into a hard crash. Fixes microsoft/vscode\#333230 Recommended reviewer: `@connor4312` ### Culprit Commit `c2b336daae7101676f179b30f92641cdfcc6b38c` — "list: batch dynamic height measurements (#330967)" by Connor Peet (`connor4312`), 2026-08-18. This commit falls within the reported regression range (`0d0c8a6...68161d9`, 1.134.0-insider → 1.135.0-insider) and introduced `probeDynamicHeights`, which allocates `new Array(range.end - range.start)` without guaranteeing `end >= start`. ### Code Flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[layout / setScrollDimensions with renderHeight <= 0] --> B[onScroll] B --> C[_rerender] C --> D["getVisibleRange(renderTop, renderHeight)"] D --> E["end = indexAfter(renderTop + renderHeight - 1)
can be < start when renderHeight ≤ 0"] E --> F["inverted IRange: end < start"] F --> G["probeDynamicHeights(range)"] G --> H["new Array(range.end - range.start)
negative length"] H --> I["RangeError: Invalid array length"] ``` ### Affected Files - `src/vs/base/browser/ui/list/listView.ts` — `getVisibleRange` (producer of the inverted range) and `probeDynamicHeights` (crash site). ### Repro Steps Not reliably reproducible via manual steps; occurs under a layout race. Conceptually: 1. Host a `ListView` inside a widget whose container can be laid out with zero/negative height (e.g., a collapsed chat/inline-chat widget). 2. Trigger a layout/scroll pass while `renderHeight <= 0`. 3. `getVisibleRange` returns an inverted range; `probeDynamicHeights` allocates a negative-length array and throws `RangeError: Invalid array length`. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `src/vs/base/browser/ui/list/listView.ts`, `getVisibleRange`: compute `start` first, then clamp `end` with `Math.max(start, indexAfter(renderTop + renderHeight - 1))`. This fixes the bug at the data producer rather than at the crash site: `getVisibleRange` constructs the `IRange`, so enforcing the `start <= end` invariant there guarantees every consumer (including `probeDynamicHeights`) receives a well-formed range. An empty range (`start === end`) is valid and yields a zero-length array, restoring the harmless behavior the previous `for`-loop had. After this change, `getVisibleRange` cannot produce a range with `end < start` because `end` is explicitly clamped to be at least `start`, so `range.end - range.start` is always `>= 0` and `new Array(...)` can no longer receive a negative length. **Alternatives considered:** - Guard at the crash site in `probeDynamicHeights` (e.g., early-return or clamp the array length there) — rejected because it patches the symptom at the bottom of the stack while leaving the malformed `IRange` flowing to every other consumer; the fix must live where the invalid data is produced. ### Recommended Owner `connor4312` (Connor Peet) — authored the culprit commit `c2b336daae71` and is an active repository collaborator with recent commits. > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/33202685801) · opus48 · 452.1 AIC · ⌖ 11.3 AIC · ⊞ 18.6K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests) --- > [!NOTE] > This was originally intended as a pull request, but PR creation failed. The changes have been pushed to the branch [`fix/listview-invalid-array-length-333230-c6490afebd6733ec`](https://github.com/vscodebot-pr/vscode/tree/fix/listview-invalid-array-length-333230-c6490afebd6733ec). > > **Original error:** ERR_API: [2026-08-28T19:30:03.784Z] create pull request in microsoft/vscode failed (attempt 1) Original error: Validation Failed: {"resource":"PullRequest","code":"custom","field":"fork_collab","message":"fork_collab Fork collab can't be granted by someone without permission"} - https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#create-a-pull-request Retryable: false Suggestion: This error cannot be resolved by retrying. Please check the error details and fix the underlying issue. Clamp it so consumers always receive `end >= start`. + end: Math.max(start, this.rangeMap.indexAfter(renderTop + renderHeight - 1)) }; } -- 2.54.0 ```

title: fix: revive telemetryInfo.sessionResource on chat editing timeline restore (fixes #333229)
body:
### Summary `isAgentHostSessionResource(this._telemetryInfo.sessionResource)` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'scheme')` because `sessionResource` is `undefined`, violating its non-nullable `readonly sessionResource: URI` contract. The invalid value originates when a chat editing session's **checkpoint timeline** is persisted and restored: the telemetry info objects are getter-backed anonymous class instances, and `JSON.stringify` drops their prototype getters, so the restored objects lack `sessionResource`. The snapshot restore path already re-injects the session resource, but the timeline restore path did not. This fix re-injects the owning `chatSessionResource` into timeline-restored telemetry info, mirroring the snapshot path. Fixes microsoft/vscode\#333229 Recommended reviewer: `@connor4312` ### Culprit Commit `8f4fc8d3273653bfb73b8d4c3cfc7eeecd00722c` — "chat: identify Agent Host telemetry sessions (#332000)" by Connor Peet (copeet@microsoft.com), Aug 21 2026. This commit introduced the `isAgentHostSessionResource(this._telemetryInfo.sessionResource)` call in `chatEditingModifiedFileEntry.ts`, which newly dereferences `.scheme` on a `sessionResource` that can be `undefined` after a timeline restore. Shipped in commit `08d4889f9ec4a1685d257b9b95de036c8e1ce1e5` (Version 1.135.0, last seen Aug 27 2026); the culprit (Aug 21) is an ancestor of the shipped build (Aug 27). ### Code Flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[_getTelemetryInfoForModel
chatEditingSession.ts:1030] -->|anonymous class
getter-based sessionResource| B[telemetryInfo on operations & fileBaselines] B --> C[getStateForPersistence
chatEditingCheckpointTimelineImpl.ts] C -->|JSON.stringify drops
prototype getters| D[persisted timeline state
sessionResource lost] D --> E[restoreFromState
operations/baselines rehydrated
sessionResource = undefined] E --> F[_notifyAction
chatEditingModifiedFileEntry.ts:277] F --> G[isAgentHostSessionResource
chatSessionsService.ts:405] G -->|resource.scheme| H[TypeError: reading 'scheme'] ``` ### Affected Files - `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatEditing/chatEditingCheckpointTimelineImpl.ts` — timeline restore path; the fix re-injects `sessionResource` here. - `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatEditing/chatEditingModifiedFileEntry.ts` (crash site, line 277) — unchanged; not the correct fix location. - `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/chatSessionsService.ts` (line 405, throw site) — unchanged. - `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatEditing/chatEditingSession.ts` (line 1030, producer of getter-based telemetry info) — unchanged. ### Repro Steps 1. Start a chat editing session that produces file operations/baselines (edits with an agent). 2. Persist the session so its checkpoint timeline state is serialized via `JSON.stringify`. 3. Reload the window so the timeline is restored via `restoreFromState`; the restored `telemetryInfo.sessionResource` is `undefined` because the getter was dropped during serialization. 4. Trigger a session action (`_notifyAction`), which calls `isAgentHostSessionResource(this._telemetryInfo.sessionResource)` → `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'scheme')`. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** (`chatEditingCheckpointTimelineImpl.ts`): In `restoreFromState`, restored `operations` (Create ops) and `fileBaselines` now pass their `telemetryInfo` through a new `_reviveTelemetryInfo` helper that re-injects the timeline's own `chatSessionResource` when `sessionResource` is missing. This fixes the data at the restore boundary — the actual producer of the invalid value — rather than guarding the crash site. The bypass is the `JSON.stringify` round-trip that silently drops the getter-backed `sessionResource` (declared non-nullable `URI`), and the restore boundary is where the type contract must be re-established. This mirrors the existing snapshot restore path, which already re-injects `this._chatSessionResource`. After this change, `restoreFromState` cannot yield a `telemetryInfo` with an undefined `sessionResource`, because every restored operation/baseline telemetry info is passed through `_reviveTelemetryInfo`, which substitutes the timeline's `chatSessionResource` whenever the deserialized value is missing. **Alternatives considered:** - Add `?.` / a guard at the crash site (`chatEditingModifiedFileEntry.ts:277`) — rejected because it masks the symptom at the consumer instead of fixing the data producer, leaving `sessionResource` `undefined` for every other consumer and violating the non-nullable contract silently. - Change the producer `_getTelemetryInfoForModel` to use own enumerable properties instead of getters — rejected because the getters are intentional (the response result is not available when editing starts), and it would not repair already-persisted state. ### Recommended Owner `@connor4312` (Connor Peet) — author of the culprit commit `8f4fc8d3`, active collaborator (recent commit Aug 27 2026), and owner of the Agent Host telemetry session code. > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/33202683766) · opus48 · 623.6 AIC · ⌖ 12 AIC · ⊞ 18.6K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests) --- > [!NOTE] > This was originally intended as a pull request, but PR creation failed. title: Test: Agents chat backgrounds
body: Refs: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/332435 - [x] macOS @Yoyokrazy - [x] windows @hediet - [x] linux @rzhao271 Complexity: 3 [Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23333232%0A%0A&assignees=TylerLeonhardt) --- ## Context Agents window chat can now sit on a decorative background instead of a flat panel color. You pick either the built-in Codicons pattern or an image of your own, with one choice for dark themes and another for light themes, and the transcript adjusts so text stays readable on top of it. ## TL;DR Turn on a chat background, live with it for a while, and tell me whether it stays out of the way. Is anything harder to read? Does the picker do what you expect? Does it land as tasteful or as gaudy? Trust your gut here. If you'd rather just poke at it, skip the rest of this. ## Prereqs Open the Agents window with `Chat: Open Agents Window` (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+A). Everything below lives there, and regular editor chat should be untouched, so it's worth one glance to confirm that. Have an image on disk ready for the second half. Any `png`, `jpg`, `gif`, `svg`, or `webp` works. ## Start with Codicons Run `Chat: Set Background...` and pick **Codicons**. You should get a faint scatter of icons behind the chat. * Resize the window a lot. The pattern regenerates at the new size, so watch for reflow that stutters or icons bunching at the edges. * Send a message. The background should hold steady through the jump from the composer to the transcript. * Right-click empty chat space on the new session view. The background commands live there too, alongside the aquarium toggle. Turn the fish on and check they swim above the background and below the chat. ## Bring your own image Run `Chat: Set Background...` again, pick **Image...**, then use `Chat: Change Background Layout...` to place it. Eleven layouts: Repeat, Stretch, Center, plus every edge and corner. Arrowing through the list previews each one live, Enter saves, Escape restores what you had. * Try a small tiling texture and then a large photo. Do the layout names match what you actually get? * Is the live preview helpful, or is the flicker more annoying than useful? * Open `Chat: Set Background...` once more. Images you've used appear under **recently used**, up to five, stored on this machine only. ## Dark and light get separate backgrounds There are two settings, one for dark themes and one for light themes. Every dark theme shares the first, every light theme shares the second. * Set something while in Dark Modern, then switch to Solarized Dark. The background should carry over, since both are dark. * Now switch to Light Modern. The chat goes back to plain, because the light setting is still empty. Is that split what you'd expect, or would you rather one image applied everywhere? * Switch to a high contrast theme. Backgrounds are suppressed there deliberately, and all three commands vanish from the Command Palette and the context menu. * `Chat: Clear Background` only clears the side you're currently on, dark or light. ## Reading over a background This is where I most want opinions. Your request bubble stays fully opaque. The assistant's response gets a mostly opaque fill that fades to nothing through the padding on either side, while wide content like terminal output and markdown tables stays fully backed. * Read a long response with code blocks, a table, and terminal output. Anything you have to squint at? * Point a busy high-contrast photo at it. That's the worst case. Where does it fall apart first? * Watch the composer, the pills above it, and the sticky headers while you scroll. Do they read as part of the chat, or as widgets floating on wallpaper? ## Notes * Settings are `chat.agentSessions.preferredDarkBackgroundImage`, `chat.agentSessions.preferredLightBackgroundImage`, and `chat.agentSessions.backgroundImageLayout`. The two image settings are machine-scoped and don't sync. The layout does. * This shipped across #332435, #332462, #332569, #332660, #332762, #332875, and #333061. * I have no known issues to exclude, so file whatever you hit.

title: fix: fall back to in-process diff when worker creation fails (fixes #333223)
body:
### Summary `new Worker(...)` throws `EINVAL` when the copilot-chat extension host tries to spin up the diff worker thread on some win32 machines (worker threads unavailable/blocked). `DiffServiceImpl` caches this construction error in a `Lazy`, so every subsequent `computeDiff` call permanently rejects even though an identical in-process diff implementation already ships. The rejection escapes through the edit-survival telemetry path (`stringEditFromDiff` → `EditCollector.getEdits` → `startReporter`'s un-`catch`ed async IIFE) as an unhandled error, affecting 24 users on 0.62.0. Fixes microsoft/vscode#333223 Recommended reviewer: `@chrmarti` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | [`3b795b1e583`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/3b795b1e58326cf6c70a7d39270981ce2c885128) | | Author | `@chrmarti` | | PR | #807 | | Message | Extract `@vscode/chat-lib` (#807) | | Why | This commit introduced the `_useWorker` split in `DiffServiceImpl.computeDiff` (lines 46-48), routing diffs through `this._worker.value.proxy.computeDiff`. When `new Worker` throws `EINVAL`, the `Lazy` caches the error and the worker branch re-throws on every call, with no fallback to the already-present in-process branch — turning an environmental worker-thread failure into a permanent, unhandled rejection. This is an ancestor of the shipped commit `08d4889`. | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Reporter as EditSurvivalTrackerService.startReporter participant Collector as EditCollector.getEdits participant Edit as stringEditFromDiff participant Diff as DiffServiceImpl.computeDiff participant Lazy as Lazy participant Worker as new Worker Reporter->>Collector: getEdits() Collector->>Edit: stringEditFromDiff(...) Edit->>Diff: computeDiff(original, modified, opts) Note over Diff: ⚠️ Root cause:
worker branch with no fallback Diff->>Lazy: this._worker.value Lazy->>Worker: new Worker(workerPath) Note over Worker: 💥 EINVAL thrown
(worker threads unavailable) Worker-->>Reporter: unhandled rejection (no catch in startReporter IIFE) ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `extensions/copilot/src/util/node/worker.ts` | crash site | L90: `this.worker = new Worker(workerPath, workerOptions)` throws EINVAL | | `extensions/copilot/src/platform/diff/node/diffServiceImpl.ts` | root cause | L46-48: `this._useWorker ? await this._worker.value.proxy.computeDiff(...) : await diffWorker.computeDiff(...)` — worker branch has no fallback when construction fails | | `extensions/copilot/src/util/vs/base/common/lazy.ts` | error amplifier | L37-50: caches the executor error and re-throws it on every `.value` access | | `extensions/copilot/src/platform/editSurvivalTracking/common/editSurvivalTrackerService.ts` | escape path | L62-70: `startReporter` async IIFE has `try/finally` but no `catch`, so the diff rejection becomes an unhandled error | ### Repro Steps 1. Run VS Code + copilot-chat 0.62.0 on a win32 environment where `worker_threads` construction fails (`new Worker` throws `EINVAL`, e.g. constrained/locked-down hosts). 2. Trigger an AI edit so edit-survival tracking starts (`startReporter`), which calls `EditCollector.getEdits()` → `stringEditFromDiff` → `DiffServiceImpl.computeDiff`. 3. The first `computeDiff` constructs the `Lazy` worker; `new Worker` throws `EINVAL`, the error is cached, and the promise rejects. 4. Because the `startReporter` IIFE has no `catch`, the rejection surfaces as `unhandlederror-EINVAL`. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** (`extensions/copilot/src/platform/diff/node/diffServiceImpl.ts` → `computeDiff()`): resolve the lazy worker inside a `try/catch` in `computeDiff`. If worker construction throws (e.g. `EINVAL`), disable the worker (`this._useWorker = false`) and fall back to the in-process `diffWorker.computeDiff`, which produces identical results (both branches call the same `computeDiffSync` logic). This is a data-producer fix: the diff service is the producer of the rejected promise, and the worker is only a performance optimization with an already-shipping in-process equivalent. The `catch` is scoped strictly to worker *construction* (`this._worker.value`) — actual diff-computation errors from `worker.proxy.computeDiff` still propagate, so no genuine error is swallowed and no `logService.error` call is removed. **Alternatives considered**: - Add a `catch` to the `startReporter` async IIFE that logs via `logService.error`. Rejected: that only silences the symptom at the consumer/escape path and would leave the diff service permanently broken for every other consumer once the worker fails to construct, degrading all diff-dependent functionality instead of transparently falling back. - Guard `new Worker` inside `worker.ts`. Rejected: `WorkerWithRpcProxy` is a generic RPC primitive; swallowing construction failures there would hide real misconfiguration from other callers, whereas `DiffServiceImpl` is the specific consumer that has a correct in-process fallback. ### Recommended Owner `@chrmarti` — author of culprit commit #807, which introduced the `_useWorker` worker/in-process split in `DiffServiceImpl`; core VS Code maintainer with recent activity. > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/33201025964) · opus48 · 425.9 AIC · ⌖ 11.7 AIC · ⊞ 18.6K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests)

title: fix: fall back to in-process diff when worker creation fails (fixes #333223)
body:
### Summary `new Worker(...)` throws `EINVAL` when the copilot-chat extension host tries to spin up the diff worker thread on some win32 machines (worker threads unavailable/blocked). `DiffServiceImpl` caches this construction error in a `Lazy`, so every subsequent `computeDiff` call permanently rejects even though an identical in-process diff implementation already ships. The rejection escapes through the edit-survival telemetry path (`stringEditFromDiff` → `EditCollector.getEdits` → `startReporter`'s un-`catch`ed async IIFE) as an unhandled error, affecting 24 users on 0.62.0. Fixes microsoft/vscode\#333223 Recommended reviewer: `@chrmarti` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | [`3b795b1e583`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/3b795b1e58326cf6c70a7d39270981ce2c885128) | | Author | `@chrmarti` | | PR | #807 | | Message | Extract `@vscode/chat-lib` (#807) | | Why | This commit introduced the `_useWorker` split in `DiffServiceImpl.computeDiff` (lines 46-48), routing diffs through `this._worker.value.proxy.computeDiff`. When `new Worker` throws `EINVAL`, the `Lazy` caches the error and the worker branch re-throws on every call, with no fallback to the already-present in-process branch — turning an environmental worker-thread failure into a permanent, unhandled rejection. This is an ancestor of the shipped commit `08d4889`. | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Reporter as EditSurvivalTrackerService.startReporter participant Collector as EditCollector.getEdits participant Edit as stringEditFromDiff participant Diff as DiffServiceImpl.computeDiff participant Lazy as Lazy participant Worker as new Worker Reporter->>Collector: getEdits() Collector->>Edit: stringEditFromDiff(...) Edit->>Diff: computeDiff(original, modified, opts) Note over Diff: ⚠️ Root cause:
worker branch with no fallback Diff->>Lazy: this._worker.value Lazy->>Worker: new Worker(workerPath) Note over Worker: 💥 EINVAL thrown
(worker threads unavailable) Worker-->>Reporter: unhandled rejection (no catch in startReporter IIFE) ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `extensions/copilot/src/util/node/worker.ts` | crash site | L90: `this.worker = new Worker(workerPath, workerOptions)` throws EINVAL | | `extensions/copilot/src/platform/diff/node/diffServiceImpl.ts` | root cause | L46-48: `this._useWorker ? await this._worker.value.proxy.computeDiff(...) : await diffWorker.computeDiff(...)` — worker branch has no fallback when construction fails | | `extensions/copilot/src/util/vs/base/common/lazy.ts` | error amplifier | L37-50: caches the executor error and re-throws it on every `.value` access | | `extensions/copilot/src/platform/editSurvivalTracking/common/editSurvivalTrackerService.ts` | escape path | L62-70: `startReporter` async IIFE has `try/finally` but no `catch`, so the diff rejection becomes an unhandled error | ### Repro Steps 1. Run VS Code + copilot-chat 0.62.0 on a win32 environment where `worker_threads` construction fails (`new Worker` throws `EINVAL`, e.g. constrained/locked-down hosts). 2. Trigger an AI edit so edit-survival tracking starts (`startReporter`), which calls `EditCollector.getEdits()` → `stringEditFromDiff` → `DiffServiceImpl.computeDiff`. 3. The first `computeDiff` constructs the `Lazy` worker; `new Worker` throws `EINVAL`, the error is cached, and the promise rejects. 4. Because the `startReporter` IIFE has no `catch`, the rejection surfaces as `unhandlederror-EINVAL`. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** (`extensions/copilot/src/platform/diff/node/diffServiceImpl.ts` → `computeDiff()`): resolve the lazy worker inside a `try/catch` in `computeDiff`. If worker construction throws (e.g. `EINVAL`), disable the worker (`this._useWorker = false`) and fall back to the in-process `diffWorker.computeDiff`, which produces identical results (both branches call the same `computeDiffSync` logic). This is a data-producer fix: the diff service is the producer of the rejected promise, and the worker is only a performance optimization with an already-shipping in-process equivalent. The `catch` is scoped strictly to worker *construction* (`this._worker.value`) — actual diff-computation errors from `worker.proxy.computeDiff` still propagate, so no genuine error is swallowed and no `logService.error` call is removed. **Alternatives considered**: - Add a `catch` to the `startReporter` async IIFE that logs via `logService.error`. Rejected: that only silences the symptom at the consumer/escape path and would leave the diff service permanently broken for every other consumer once the worker fails to construct, degrading all diff-dependent functionality instead of transparently falling back. - Guard `new Worker` inside `worker.ts`. Rejected: `WorkerWithRpcProxy` is a generic RPC primitive; swallowing construction failures there would hide real misconfiguration from other callers, whereas `DiffServiceImpl` is the specific consumer that has a correct in-process fallback. ### Recommended Owner `@chrmarti` — author of culprit commit #807, which introduced the `_useWorker` worker/in-process split in `DiffServiceImpl`; core VS Code maintainer with recent activity. > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/33201025964) · opus48 · 425.9 AIC · ⌖ 11.7 AIC · ⊞ 18.6K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests) --- > [!NOTE] > This was originally intended as a pull request, but PR creation failed. title: fix: defer terminal tool confirmation editor layout to next animation frame (fixes #333221)
body:
### Summary `ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications` is firing across the chat confirmation surface. The synthetic browser warning carries only non-causal delivery context (`ResizeObserverLoopContext(...)`) listing the wrapped observers that ran in the same rendering frame — the browser does not expose the actual observer that skipped a delivery. Among the listed observers, the one that synchronously writes layout back into its own observed element is `ChatTerminalToolConfirmationSubPart.editor`, which calls `editor.object.layout(width)` inside the resize callback; that write flexes the embedded editor's height back into the observed `elements.editor`, re-entering the same observation phase and tripping the loop warning under bursty resizes. Impact: noisy unhandled-error telemetry (spike on `1.136.0-insider`), no functional break. Fixes microsoft/vscode#333221 Recommended reviewer: `@bryanchen-d` ### Culprit Commit No single culprit commit introduced this regression. The observers named in the bucket context (`BaseChatConfirmationWidget.message`, `BaseChatConfirmationWidget.messageContent`, `ChatInputPart.containerHeight`, `ChatTerminalToolConfirmationSubPart.editor`, `ChatThinkingContentPart.wrapper`, `ChatToolConfirmationCarouselPart.contentExpansion`) all pre-date the `08d4889f...3fcbd108` regression window — a `-S` search for each name inside the range returns nothing. The `[ResizeObserverLoopContext(...)]` bucketing format itself was introduced in #328065 (Jul 29), also before the window. This is the same self-feeding pattern previously fixed for `ChatInputPart.containerHeight` in [#316524](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/316524) (fixes \#316509), recurring in a sibling widget. The spike is best explained by increased exercise of the terminal tool confirmation surface rather than a new triggering commit, so the bug is treated as pre-existing and the fix is applied at the self-feeding write site. ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Browser as Browser layout participant Observer as ChatTerminalToolConfirmationSubPart.editor observer participant Editor as editor.object participant Site as elements.editor (observed) Browser->>Observer: deliver resize entry (width) Note over Observer: ⚠️ Root cause:
synchronous editor.object.layout(width) Observer->>Editor: layout(width) Editor->>Site: height flexes back into observed element Site->>Browser: resize re-entered in same phase Note over Browser: 💥 ResizeObserver loop completed
with undelivered notifications ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/toolInvocationParts/chatTerminalToolConfirmationSubPart.ts` | root cause / fix | L194-L200 (pre-fix): `new DisposableResizeObserver('ChatTerminalToolConfirmationSubPart.editor', entries => { ... editor.object.layout(width); })` — synchronous layout write into the observed element | | `src/vs/base/browser/dom.ts` | context provider | L2169-L2184: `getRecentDisposableResizeObserverContextForLoopError` — names are delivery context only, "not causal attribution" | | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/input/chatInputPart.ts` | precedent fix | L4022-L4036: prior rAF-deferral fix for the identical pattern (#316524) | ### Repro Steps 1. Start a chat session and trigger a terminal tool confirmation so the `ChatTerminalToolConfirmationSubPart` embedded editor renders. 2. Rapidly resize the chat panel / window (or stream content that repeatedly changes the editor width) so the editor width observer fires in bursts. 3. Observe the `ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications` warning surface in error telemetry. It is timing-dependent; bursty width changes within a single rendering frame increase the likelihood of the browser skipping a delivery. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — In `chatTerminalToolConfirmationSubPart.ts`, the resize callback no longer calls `editor.object.layout(width)` synchronously. It records the last observed width and schedules the layout on the next animation frame via an `AnimationFrameScheduler` (disposed with the part). Deferring the layout write out of the resize-observation phase breaks the self-feeding loop while preserving the resize behavior — the editor still lays out to the observed width, just one frame later. This fixes the problem at the site that produces the feedback write (the self-resizing layout call), not at a crash site or by suppressing the warning, and it reuses the exact pattern already proven for `ChatInputPart.containerHeight` in #316524. **Alternatives considered** — Wrapping the layout call in `try/catch` was rejected because the warning is delivered as a stackless `ErrorEvent` on `window`, not thrown at the call site, so a local catch would not suppress it and would hide nothing useful. Widening or muting the telemetry context in `dom.ts` was rejected because that helper is intentionally non-causal delivery context and other observers legitimately rely on it. ### Recommended Owner `@bryanchen-d` — authored the precedent fix [#316524](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/316524) and the ResizeObserver delivery-context telemetry (#328065, #2613d4a naming), owns the chat confirmation widget area, and is the current issue assignee. > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/33200593327) · opus48 · 418.4 AIC · ⌖ 12.3 AIC · ⊞ 18.6K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests)

with undelivered notifications ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/toolInvocationParts/chatTerminalToolConfirmationSubPart.ts` | root cause / fix | L194-L200 (pre-fix): `new DisposableResizeObserver('ChatTerminalToolConfirmationSubPart.editor', entries => { ... editor.object.layout(width); })` — synchronous layout write into the observed element | | `src/vs/base/browser/dom.ts` | context provider | L2169-L2184: `getRecentDisposableResizeObserverContextForLoopError` — names are delivery context only, "not causal attribution" | | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/input/chatInputPart.ts` | precedent fix | L4022-L4036: prior rAF-deferral fix for the identical pattern (#316524) | ### Repro Steps 1. title: Unify internal telemetry checks across processes
body:
This pull request addresses inconsistencies in how internal telemetry is marked across different processes in the application. The changes ensure that telemetry events are correctly flagged as internal based on both the user's account status and their domain.

### Key Changes:
- **Agent Host Process**: Updated `AgentHostTelemetryService` to include the Copilot signal when determining if telemetry should be marked as internal. This ensures that internal Copilot users are correctly identified regardless of their domain.
- **Dynamic Internal Flag**: Modified `TelemetryService.msftInternal` to reflect real-time updates from common properties, rather than being a static snapshot at construction.
- **Tests Added**: Introduced new tests to validate the changes in both `agentHostTelemetryService.test.ts` and `telemetryService.test.ts`, ensuring that the new logic is covered and functions as expected.
- **Documentation**: Cleaned up comments and documentation to clarify the purpose of changes and correct any inaccuracies.

These updates enhance the reliability of telemetry data and ensure consistent behavior across all processes, addressing previous gaps in internal user identification.

title: Fix chat model visibility issue for unrenderable identifiers
body:
Fix https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/333188

This pull request addresses the visibility issue for chat models that are unrenderable, specifically for users who have previously stored unrenderable model IDs.

  - Removed redundant code that was previously attempting to prune stale entries.
- Added regression tests to ensure that the `Auto` model behaves correctly and that users can recover from stale states.

### Key Points:
- The changes reduce the risk of drift between the editor and service layers, which was the root cause of the original issue.
- The overall production diff is now more concise, with a focus on clarity and correctness.
- All tests pass successfully, confirming that the functionality is intact and the issue is resolved.

title: accounts: preserve sign-in during session replacement
body:
## Summary

- Keeps the default account signed in while GitHub authentication replaces a session in a combined event.
- Prevents the Agent Host sign-in banner from appearing during an active session when the replacement credential remains valid.
- Adds privacy-safe diagnostics that distinguish interactive-login replacements from shared secret-storage reconciliation.
- Preserves immediate sign-out behavior for removal-only events, including while replacement reconciliation is in flight.

Fixes #333197

<details>
<summary>Technical context for AI-assisted review</summary>

### Intent and previous behavior

GitHub Authentication can publish one session-change event containing both the removed current session and its replacement. The default-account listener treated the removal as a complete sign-out, cleared the account, and skipped reconciliation. That temporary null account propagated through chat entitlement state and caused the Agent Host sign-in banner to appear even though the replacement credential was valid.

Runtime logs from the reported occurrence show the GitHub removal and addition in the same event cycle, followed within milliseconds by the Sessions signed-out path. Subsequent authentication using the replacement credential succeeded.

### Implementation

The default-account listener now distinguishes removal-only events from events containing added or changed replacement candidates. Removal-only events still clear the account immediately. Replacement events retain the current account while the existing throttled refresh retrieves, validates, and selects the actual default session.

Each asynchronous refresh captures the current session before it starts. If that session changes while the refresh is pending, the stale result is discarded so an earlier replacement reconciliation cannot overwrite a later removal-only sign-out.

GitHub Authentication records replacement events at info level with only the source category, event kind, and added/removed/changed counts. Routine session changes remain at trace level. The logs intentionally exclude account labels and identifiers, session identifiers, scopes, and credentials.

Regression coverage drives a combined replacement and a genuine removal-only event through the authentication service fixture. A blocked-refresh case verifies that removal remains final when replacement reconciliation was already in flight.

### Behavior and constraints

- Added or changed sessions are reconciliation candidates; they are not assigned directly.
- If reconciliation finds no valid replacement, the normal refresh clears the default account.
- Events from unrelated authentication providers remain ignored.
- This change addresses the false default-account transition and sign-in banner. Remote Agent Host tunnel reconnect churn from the same authentication event remains separate follow-up work.

</details>

title: `Repository.setConfig()` in the built-in Git extension always uses `git config --add`, causing unbounded duplicate branch config entries
body:
Type: Bug --- ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Open a workspace containing a git repository, with the built-in **Git** extension enabled (default) and the **GitHub Pull Requests and Issues** extension installed and signed in. 2. Check out a local branch that has an associated GitHub pull request (e.g. via "Checkout" from the GitHub Pull Requests view, or by opening a branch that already has an open PR). 3. Cause the extension host to reactivate several times while that branch stays checked out — e.g.: - Run **Developer: Reload Window** a few times, or - Reconnect a Remote-SSH / Remote-WSL / Codespaces session a few times (each reconnect restarts the extension host), or - Switch away from and back to the branch a few times. 4. Open a terminal in the repo and run: ``` git config --get-all branch..github-pr-owner-number ``` **Actual result:** The same value is listed multiple times — once per reactivation/association event. The duplicate count grows without bound the more the association logic re-runs (in a long-lived Remote session this can reach dozens or more identical lines for a single branch). The `.git/config` file for that branch section looks like: ``` [branch "feat/example"] remote = origin merge = refs/heads/feat/example github-pr-owner-number = "Owner#repo#42" github-pr-owner-number = "Owner#repo#42" github-pr-owner-number = "Owner#repo#42" ... ``` If the branch's associated PR number later changes (e.g. old PR closed, new PR opened for the same branch), the *old* value is never removed — it just keeps appending new duplicate lines for the new value on top of the stale ones, so both stale and current values remain physically present in config. **Expected result:** Setting a config value for a key that already has exactly one value should **replace** that value, not add an additional line. There should only ever be one `branch..github-pr-owner-number` entry per branch (unless something intentionally wants a multi-valued key). ### Root cause (found via source inspection) `extensions/git/dist/main.js` implements the public `Repository.setConfig(key, value)` API as an unconditional append: ```js setConfig(e,t){return this.run(ae.Config(!1),()=>this.repository.config("add","local",e,t))} ``` This always shells out to `git config --add`, never `git config --replace-all` (or a check-existing-then-overwrite). Any extension that calls `repository.setConfig(...)` to persist a value tied to a branch — such as the GitHub Pull Requests extension writing `branch..github-pr-owner-number` every time it associates a branch with its PR — will accumulate duplicate lines every time that code path re-runs (extension activation, branch switch, PR metadata refresh, etc.), rather than keeping a single up-to-date value. ### Impact **1. PR-comment/active-PR flakiness (your original symptom) — most direct impact.** The GitHub Pull Requests extension parses `branch..github-pr-owner-number` to decide which PR a checked-out branch belongs to, and that's what drives whether it fetches and overlays that PR's review comments inline. We directly observed `caddie-gateway`'s `feat/power-platform` branch carrying **two different PR numbers** (`#19` then `#21`) simultaneously in config before cleanup. Whether the extension resolves the "correct" one is just an accident of parse order/timing/caching, not a guarantee — which is exactly consistent with comments sometimes rendering and sometimes not, without you changing anything. **2. Silent failure of any future cleanup by the config's own owner.** I tested this directly: once a key has 2+ values, `git config --unset ` (without `--unset-all`) **refuses to run**: ``` warning: test.key has multiple values exit code: 5 ``` So if the GitHub Pull Requests extension (or VS Code core) ever tries to *clear* a stale PR association — e.g. when a branch's linked PR is closed/merged and it wants to remove the entry — that unset call fails and does nothing, leaving the stale value permanently stuck alongside future duplicates. The bug isn't just "extra lines get added," it's also "the normal cleanup path can never fix it once it's already duplicated." **3. Unbounded, compounding growth over the life of a workspace.** Because the trigger is extension-host reactivation (window reloads, Remote-SSH/WSL reconnects, branch re-visits) rather than a one-time event, the duplicate count has no ceiling. We saw this scale from single digits up to 69 lines for one branch in a workspace that's only been active for one PR cycle — in a long-lived remote dev environment this will keep growing indefinitely, making the problem worse the longer you leave a branch checked out. **4. Broader blast radius than just this one key.** The same `Repository.setConfig()` API is used for other branch-scoped values too (e.g. `github-pr-base-branch`, which we also saw duplicated in `caddie-config-repo`). Any extension — not just GitHub Pull Requests — that calls this VS Code API to persist per-branch state is subject to the same silent accumulation, so this isn't a narrowly-scoped one-extension issue; it's a defect in a shared core API. ### Suggested fix `Repository.setConfig()` should behave like a "set" (overwrite) operation — either check for an existing single value and use `--replace-all`, or default to that flag — rather than unconditionally calling `git config --add`. title: Render session artifact locations as paths and centre the artifacts file icon
body:
## Description

Artifact and reference pills in the agents window showed raw URIs (`file:///c:/Users/besimmonds/.copilot/session-state/be29001b-.../files/ab-windows.json`), and the themed file icon in the artifacts dropdown sat ~3px above the row's centre.

### Location text (`sessionArtifacts.ts`)

- `sessionArtifactLocationText` renders locations through `ILabelService.getUriLabel(uri, { relative: true })`: no scheme, tildified under the user home, native separators/drive letters (`vscode-agent-host` URIs via their registered formatter), relative to the session's folder.
- Only file-system schemes (`file`, `vscode-remote`, `vscode-userdata`, `vscode-agent-host`) become paths. Links and agent-supplied custom schemes keep their whole URI — a path label drops the scheme, authority and query, which would make them read like files that are nowhere to be found.
- A location that *is* the workspace folder has no relative label (`''`), so it falls back to its full path instead of an empty hover.
- The sections observable re-reads on `onDidChangeFormatters` and `onDidChangeWorkspaceFolders`, since the session's folder is mounted a moment after the session becomes active.

```
file:///home/alice/repo/src/app.ts   ->  src/app.ts
file:///home/alice/notes.md          ->  ~/notes.md
myapp://team/board?id=42             ->  myapp://team/board?id=42   (unchanged)
```

### Icon centring (`chatPills.css`)

- The existing rule targeted `.action-widget .action-list-item .icon.file-icon` — a class the action widget never puts on its rows — so it never applied, and the sizing sat on the wrong element (themed file icons paint through `::before`).
- Now targets `.monaco-list-row.action`, gives the icon slot the action row's height and centres the glyph inside it. Codicons are unaffected because `codicon.css` already sets `line-height: 1`; this restores the same for font- and image-based file icon themes.
- `chatDropdownPill` is the only producer of `file-icon` classes for action lists, so the newly matching selector stays scoped to chat pill dropdowns.

### Supporting

- `componentFixtures/fixtureUtils.ts` registers `IWorkspaceContextService`, needed now that `SessionArtifacts` declares it under the strict test instantiation service.
- New unit coverage for the location text; existing artifact tests pass a label service stub.

The Output panel shows the AgentHost component repeatedly failing to resolve a GitHub token, even though a valid GitHub authentication session is provably persisted locally via the standard vscode.github-authentication provider. ### Steps to reproduce Sign in to GitHub in VS Code via Accounts menu (standard OAuth flow or device code flow — both attempted). Confirm a session exists: querying state.vscdb's ItemTable shows a populated (1059-byte) entry for secret://{"extensionId":"vscode.github-authentication","key":"github.auth"} — i.e. authentication succeeded and persisted. Open a .cs (or any) file and type to trigger inline completions. Observe Output → Window. ### Expected behavior AgentHost resolves a token from the existing github-authentication session and Copilot completions/ghost text appear. ### Actual behavior Initial state (before further troubleshooting): AgentHost logs, repeatedly and immediately on every window load and every Copilot status bar interaction: ``` [AgentHost] No token resolved for resource: https://api.github.com [AgentHost] Clearing authentication for resource: https://api.github.com [AgentHost] No token resolved for resource: https://api.github.com/repos [AgentHost] Clearing authentication for resource: https://api.github.com/repos ``` This occurred regardless of: Fresh standard OAuth sign-in Fresh device-code sign-in (github-authentication.preferDeviceCodeFlow: true) Full sign-out/sign-in cycles Full quit/restart of VS Code (not just window reload) Removing an organization's OAuth App access restrictions (the account is a member of an org that had this policy enabled; disabling it changed behavior, see below) Revoking and reauthorizing all related OAuth apps/GitHub Apps After removing the organization's OAuth App access restriction and doing a completely fresh device-code sign-in, the failure mode changed to: ``` [AgentHost] Authenticating for resource: https://api.github.com [AgentHost] Authenticating for resource: https://api.github.com/repos ``` ...with no further log output at all — no success, no failure, no timeout — and ghost text still does not appear, even after Developer: Reload Window and full app restarts performed after this point. ### Additional notes Copilot Chat itself functions normally (used throughout this entire troubleshooting session), suggesting AgentHost's token handling for completions is on a different/disconnected path from whatever Chat uses. No "GitHub Copilot" completions-specific Output channel exists in this build — only "GitHub Copilot Log (Code Reference)," which remains empty throughout. chat.agentHost.allowSignedOutWhenUsable: true was tried as a possible workaround; no observable effect.
